requirements.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 300, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. Preserve their existing positions and sizes. With speed 300 px/s and jump-speed 420 px/s, the player should be able to jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and report any concern without changing the platforms.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.
Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Player overlap changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction.
Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.
Render the player cyan (#00FFFF) to make it easier to track. Preserve its 24x32 dimensions, collision shape, and initial spawn. Preserve all other existing visual elements.
Limit the requested change to player speed 300 px/s and cyan player rendering. Preserve existing platforms, controls, jump speed, gravity, collisions, exit behavior, reset paths, fixed view, and HUD.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 300, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. Preserve their existing positions and sizes. With speed 300 px/s and jump-speed 420 px/s, the player should be able to jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and report any concern without changing the platforms.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.

Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Current player overlap during play changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction. Preserve normal victory on subsequent attempts.

Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD through the shared restart path. Clear stale exit contact during this restart.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.
Render the player cyan (#00FFFF) to make it easier to track. Preserve its 24x32 dimensions, collision shape, and initial spawn. Preserve all other existing visual elements.

Limit the requested implementation change to fixing restart and exit-contact handling for the reported reset-after-win regression. Preserve player speed 300 px/s, cyan rendering, existing platforms, controls, jump speed 420 px/s, gravity 1000 px/s², collisions, normal win behavior, both reset paths, fixed view, and HUD. Use the existing object and source bindings.

Give reset priority over other state transitions and end transition processing for the reset tick. Restart must invalidate remembered exit contact and reject overlap data or delayed contact callbacks belonging to the pre-teleport state. Returning to spawn must not trigger WON without current player contact with the exit. Contact evaluation must recover safely after physics synchronization so reaching the exit on a later attempt still wins.

Manually reach the exit using actual Left/Right and Space input, observe the normal win, and press R while won. Confirm the player returns centered at (100, 414) with zero velocity at reset, playing state, active controls, and the normal HUD. Observe subsequent physics frames without movement input: the state must remain playing at spawn despite any stale exit contact. Then complete another attempt and confirm normal victory. Repeat win/reset cycles and report any recurrence of WON at spawn, including the reported state=1 with exitOverlap=false symptom.

# Game Design Document — Bridge Runner

## Concept
A small Godot 4 GDScript side-view jump game. Move the cyan player at 300 px/s with the left/right arrow keys and jump with Space to cross three visible platforms and reach a green exit. Preserve the existing platforms and controls. Falling restarts the level, and R resets it during play or after winning. Restart must clear stale exit contact so the player remains in the playing state at spawn and can complete another attempt. Use a fixed 960x540 view, procedural shapes, one level, and no sound, external assets, plugins, or network access. Keep simulation, input actions, rendering, and interface responsibilities separate.

## Source binding for main-scene, exit, win, fall-restart, manual-reset,
## and level-state. All player simulation is stepped here after reset intent.
const OBJECT_IDS := [
	"main-scene", "exit", "win", "fall-restart", "manual-reset", "level-state"
]
const SPAWN := Vector2(100.0, 414.0)
const FALL_LIMIT := 600.0

enum LevelState { PLAYING, WON }

var state: LevelState = LevelState.PLAYING
var _exit_contact_pending: bool = false

@onready var player = $Player
@onready var input_actions = $InputActions
@onready var exit_area: Area2D = $Exit
@onready var hud = $HUD


func _ready() -> void:
	exit_area.body_entered.connect(_on_exit_body_entered)
	restart_level()


func _physics_process(delta: float) -> void:
	# manual-reset has priority over simulation and every other transition.
	if input_actions.reset_requested():
		restart_level()
		return
	if state == LevelState.WON:
		return
	player.simulate(
		delta, input_actions.horizontal_intent(), input_actions.jump_requested()
	)
	if player.global_position.y > FALL_LIMIT:
		restart_level()
		return
	if _exit_contact_pending or exit_area.overlaps_body(player):
		_win_level()


func restart_level() -> void:
	# fall-restart and manual-reset share this complete restoration path.
	state = LevelState.PLAYING
	_exit_contact_pending = false
	player.reset_to(SPAWN)
	hud.show_playing()


func _on_exit_body_entered(body: Node2D) -> void:
	if body == player and state == LevelState.PLAYING:
		# Defer the win decision to the reset-first physics step.
		_exit_contact_pending = true


func _win_level() -> void:
	state = LevelState.WON
	_exit_contact_pending = false
	player.stop_motion()
	hud.show_won()

## Object player; mechanisms horizontal-movement, jump, platform-collision.
## The controller supplies intent and owns the timing of each simulation step.
const OBJECT_ID := "player"
const MECHANISM_IDS := ["horizontal-movement", "jump", "platform-collision"]
const GRAVITY := 1000.0
const RuntimeSource = preload("res://studio/runtime.gd")

var speed: float = 0.0
var jump_speed: float = 0.0
var controls_enabled: bool = false
var _studio_runtime = RuntimeSource.new()


func reset_to(spawn: Vector2) -> void:
	global_position = spawn
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO
	# Read the authoritative fields on startup and on both restart paths.
	# Do not duplicate their defaults or ranges in game source.
	var speed_value: Variant = _studio_runtime.object_value(OBJECT_ID, "speed")
	var jump_value: Variant = _studio_runtime.object_value(OBJECT_ID, "jump-speed")
	controls_enabled = (
		(speed_value is int or speed_value is float)
		and (jump_value is int or jump_value is float)
	)
	if not controls_enabled:
		push_error("Player requires numeric speed and jump-speed fields in design/game.json.")
		return
	speed = float(speed_value)
	jump_speed = float(jump_value)


func simulate(delta: float, direction: float, jump_pressed: bool) -> void:
	if not controls_enabled:
		return
	# horizontal-movement: immediate start/stop, with no residual drift.
	velocity.x = direction * speed
	# jump: only a fresh press on a supporting platform starts a jump.
	velocity.y += GRAVITY * delta
	if jump_pressed and is_on_floor():
		velocity.y = -jump_speed
	# platform-collision: use the scene's matching solid collision rectangles.
	move_and_slide()


func stop_motion() -> void:
	controls_enabled = false
	velocity = Vector2.ZERO

## Object input-actions: keyboard bindings and intent only.

	_bind_key(&"move_right", KEY_RIGHT)
	_bind_key(&"jump", KEY_SPACE)
	_bind_key(&"reset_level", KEY_R)


func horizontal_intent() -> float:
	# Equal opposing inputs cancel, including while airborne.
	return Input.get_axis(&"move_left", &"move_right")

	return Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"jump")

	return Input.is_action_just_pressed(&"reset_level")

	if not InputMap.has_action(action):

	var event := InputEventKey.new()
	event.keycode = key
	if not InputMap.action_has_event(action, event):

userAcceptance.text: Implement one Godot 4 GDScript 2D level with procedural visuals, no sound, no external assets or plugins, and no network access. Do not perform hash checks during building.
The main-scene object is bound to scenes/main.tscn. Keep every declared object and mechanism associated with its listed source bindings.

Preserve player field IDs speed and jump-speed. Speed is editable numeric data with value 300, minimum 50, maximum 500. Jump-speed is editable numeric data with value 420, minimum 200, maximum 700. Game source reads these frozen values through StudioRuntime.object_value(). Do not modify backend-owned design/game.json or studio/runtime.gd.
Left and Right Arrow move the player horizontally; Space triggers a grounded jump; R resets the level. Opposing direction inputs cancel, and holding Space does not produce repeated jumps.

Show exactly three solid platforms simultaneously. Preserve their existing positions and sizes. With speed 300 px/s and jump-speed 420 px/s, the player should be able to jump from the starting platform to the middle platform and then to the exit platform. Manually assess reachability and report any concern without changing the platforms.
The player lands reliably on matching platform collision shapes and can fall through the open gaps. Grounded detection permits jumping only while supported.

Place a clearly visible green exit on the third platform. Current player overlap during play changes the level to won, stops player movement, and displays a win message with an R restart instruction. Preserve normal victory on subsequent attempts.

Falling below the level during play automatically restores the initial spawn, zero velocity, playing state, and normal HUD through the shared restart path. Clear stale exit contact during this restart.
R restores the same initial state during play and after winning. The player can complete another attempt after either reset path.
Use a fixed 960x540 logical view with all three platforms and the exit visible together. The view does not follow the player or scroll.
The HUD explains arrow movement, Space jumping, R reset, and the green-exit goal. Win feedback is readable and does not obscure the platform route.
Keep physics and level simulation separate from input action mapping, procedural rendering, and interface updates. Input supplies intent; rendering reflects state; HUD presents controls and outcomes.
Render the player cyan (#00FFFF) to make it easier to track. Preserve its 24x32 dimensions, collision shape, and initial spawn. Preserve all other existing visual elements.

Limit the requested implementation change to fixing restart and exit-contact handling for the reported reset-after-win regression. Preserve player speed 300 px/s, cyan rendering, existing platforms, controls, jump speed 420 px/s, gravity 1000 px/s², collisions, normal win behavior, both reset paths, fixed view, and HUD. Use the existing object and source bindings.

Give reset priority over other state transitions and end transition processing for the reset tick. Restart must invalidate remembered exit contact and reject overlap data or delayed contact callbacks belonging to the pre-teleport state. Returning to spawn must not trigger WON without current player contact with the exit. Contact evaluation must recover safely after physics synchronization so reaching the exit on a later attempt still wins.

Confirm the player returns centered at (100, 414) with zero velocity at reset, playing state, active controls, and the normal HUD. Observe subsequent physics frames without movement input: the state must remain playing at spawn despite any stale exit contact. Then complete another attempt and confirm normal victory. Repeat win/reset cycles and report any recurrence of WON at spawn, including the reported state=1 with exitOverlap=false symptom.
